discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Allan MacDonald (with R. Bistritzer) predicted from a simple continuum model that, at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become almost flat, so electron-electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's group made this real. Using a controlled tear-and-stack technique, they observed correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be tuned with a gate voltage. This founded 'twistronics', in which the twist angle becomes a new control knob for quantum matter. Moiré platforms have since shown orbital ferromagnetism, the quantized anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators and strange-metal transport, all in one tunable, clean device. Theory predicted a measurable effect and experiment confirmed it with precision. Together they opened a whole field and changed how we study strongly correlated electrons.
